== Biography ==

This page is an index for three separate men or working identities formerly combined under one biography:

{| class="wikitable sortable"
! Working identity
! Estimated dates
! Secure evidence
! Detailed page
|-
| '''John de Glasgu I'''
| Born before c.1425–30; active 1447–1455
| Glasgow burgess and witness in two civic property acts; the same individual securely crosses 1450
| [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_de_Glasgu_I%27 John de Glasgu I]
|-
| '''John Glasgw of Stirling'''
| Born before c.1455; active 1475–1479/80
| Witness in two Stirling property and religious-endowment acts
| [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_Glasgw_of_Stirling John Glasgw of Stirling]
|-
| '''John de Glasgow alias Smith / John Glasgow of Saltmarket'''
| Born before c.1485; dead before 21 October 1553
| Alias Smith acquired a Glasgow High Street annual rent in 1506; the Saltmarket owner held the same identifiable tenement in 1527 and 1548 and was dead by 1553
| [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_de_Glasgow_alias_Smith_/_John_Glasgow_of_Saltmarket%27 John de Glasgow alias Smith / John Glasgow of Saltmarket]
|}

The split avoids turning several compatible records into one implausibly long life. It also separates secure identities from proposed family relationships.

=== Core documentary findings ===

* '''John de Glasgu I''' witnessed Glasgow property acts on 21 June 1447 and 10 April 1455. Both were recorded by Henry Michael, notary and clerk of Glasgow's burgh court, and the 1447 wording places John among the burgesses of Glasgow.<ref name="John1447">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine: Munimenta Fratrum Predicatorum de Glasgu'' (Glasgow, 1846), act dated 21 June 1447; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="John1455">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 10 April 1455 in the published Latin; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>
* '''John Glasgw of Stirling''' witnessed Stirling acts dated 11 April 1475 and 2 March 1479/80. The repeated name, town and role make these two records highly likely to concern one man.<ref name="StirlingJohn">''Charters and Other Documents Relating to the Royal Burgh of Stirling, A.D. 1124–1705'' (Glasgow, 1884), abstracts dated 11 April 1475 and 2 March 1479/80; [https://archive.org/details/chartersotherdoc00stir Internet Archive].</ref>
* '''John de Glasgow alias Smith''' jointly acquired a four-shilling annual rent from a Glasgow High Street tenement on 28 April 1506.<ref name="AliasSmith">Glasgow University Archives, Blackhouse Charters, GUA BL/204, formerly GUA 16403, instrument dated 28 April 1506.</ref>
* A '''John Glasgow''' held an identifiable Saltmarket tenement in 1527 and 1548. The same four-shilling rent, street position and adjoining properties identify one continuous holding. John was described as deceased by 21 October 1553.<ref name="JohnSaltmarket1527">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 2 May 1527, recording a four-shilling annual rent from the tenement of John Glasgow; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="JohnSaltmarket1548">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', property inventory dated 5 January 1548, repeating the four-shilling annual rent, location and neighbours of John Glasgu's tenement; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="JohnDead1553">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', act dated 21 October 1553, describing John Rankyn's property as bounded by the lands of the late John Glasgow.</ref>

! Proposed identification or relationship
! Assessment
! Reason
|-
| Glasgow 1447 = Glasgow 1455
| '''Very high confidence'''
| Same name, burgh, civic role, notary and property setting
|-
| Stirling 1475 = Stirling 1479/80
| '''High confidence'''
| Same uncommon name, town and witnessing role, four years apart
|-
| Alias Smith 1506 = Saltmarket owner 1527–1548
| '''Plausible but unproved'''
| Same name, city, generation and property milieu; no repeated alias, matching property or associate
|-
| John de Glasgu I = John of Stirling
| '''Plausible but unproved'''
| Compatible chronology and civic setting; no shared property, relative, office or associate
|-
| John de Glasgu I father of John of Stirling
| '''Possible hypothesis'''
| Chronology works, but no parentage or succession record exists
|-
| John of Stirling father of Alias Smith and William Glasgow
| '''Possible hypothesis'''
| Chronology, naming and civic-property setting fit; no record calls either man his son
|-
| Alias Smith brother of William Glasgow
| '''Possible hypothesis'''
| Compatible generation and Glasgow property milieu; no stated relationship
|}

=== Hypothetical family tree ===

<small>The following tree is a research model, not a proved pedigree. Relationships above [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] and all children marked “proposed” remain unsupported by a direct parentage record.</small>

* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_de_Glasgu_I%27 '''John de Glasgu I'''] — born before c.1425; active 1447–1455
** [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_Glasgw_of_Stirling '''John Glasgw of Stirling'''] — born before c.1455; active 1475–1479/80; hypothetical son
*** [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_de_Glasgow_alias_Smith_/_John_Glasgow_of_Saltmarket%27 '''John de Glasgow alias Smith / John Glasgow of Saltmarket'''] — born before c.1485; dead before 21 October 1553; hypothetical son; combined identity plausible but unproved
*** [[Glasgow-1098|'''William Glasgow''']] — born c.1485–1495; dead before c.1543; hypothetical son; married [[Brade-232|Esbell Brade]], born c.1490–1500
**** [[Glasgow-1093|'''John Glasgow''']] — born c.1510; dead before 8 November 1575; '''proved son''' of William and Esbell; married [[Spreull-4|Jonet Spreull]], born before c.1516 and alive after 1575
**** '''James Glasgow''' — born c.1515; alive after 1571; proposed son
**** [[Glasgow-1096|'''Robert Glasgow''']] — born c.1520; alive after 1572; proposed son; married [[Rolland-239|Margaret Rolland]], born c.1535
**** '''Isobella Glasgow''' — born c.1530; alive after 27 January 1563; proposed daughter; married '''Archibald Herbison''', born c.1530
**** [[Glasgow-1097|'''Archibald Glasgow''']] — born c.1533; alive after 1560; proposed son; married [[Newlands-647|Isobell Newlands]], born c.1530

The only parent-child relationship in this model proved by a contemporary record is:

: [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] and [[Brade-232|Esbell Brade]]
:: → [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]], husband of [[Spreull-4|Jonet Spreull]]

On 31 December 1534 William and Esbell transferred property to John, expressly described as their son, and to John's wife Jonet.<ref name="WilliamBradeSpreull1534">''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', protocol dated 31 December 1534, recording William Glasgow and Esbell Brade, their son John Glasgow and his wife Jonet Spreull.</ref>

=== Why the hypothetical arrangement is plausible ===

* The chronology permits John of Stirling, an adult by 1475, to have sons active in 1506 and the early sixteenth century.
* All three working identities occur in formal urban property or annual-rent records.
* John de Glasgu I appeared with Andrew Brady in 1455; John of Stirling witnessed a 1479/80 act involving property beside Gilbert Brady; Robert Brade witnessed a Spreull transaction in 1488; and William Glasgow later married Esbell Brade while their son married Jonet Spreull.
* William's proved son was named John, which is consistent with — but does not prove — William having a father named John.

The naming pattern and civic network are supporting context only. They cannot replace an explicit term such as ''filius'', ''heres'', ''frater'', ''relicta'' or ''proximior de sanguine''.

=== What is not proved ===

* John de Glasgu I and John of Stirling are not proved to be the same man or father and son.
* John of Stirling is not proved to be the father of Alias Smith or William Glasgow.
* Alias Smith and the Saltmarket owner are not proved to be one man.
* Alias Smith is not proved to be William Glasgow's brother.
* James, Robert, Isobella and Archibald are not presently proved children of William Glasgow and Esbell Brade.
* No record yet joins the fifteenth-century bearers to the proved William–John pedigree by parentage or inheritance.

=== Research priorities ===

# Transcribe GUA BL/204 in full, including witnesses, source of title, exact alias syntax and property description.
# Inspect James Darow's Stirling protocol book, B66/1/1/1, for full entries, neighbouring acts and additional appearances of John Glasgw.
# Trace the Saltmarket property immediately after John Glasgow's death between 5 January 1548 and 21 October 1553, looking for an heir, widow, assignee or nearest relative.
# Inspect the complete 1534 William–Esbell–John–Jonet protocol for witnesses, prior ownership and source of title.
# Reconstruct the Brady/Brade and Spreull families independently rather than assuming that recurring surnames identify one pedigree.
